login.note: Signed out, the home page IS the login wall — Google / Facebook / email on one card. The provider buttons open a popup rather than navigating, so the operator must keep the share open and must not close what looks like a stray window. Quora is aggressive about new-device and new-IP checks and may hold the session behind an emailed code.

logout.note: Reached through the profile menu in the top bar; the item is not in the DOM until that menu is open. A GET of https://www.quora.com/logout has historically worked but is unverified here and may simply bounce to the home wall while leaving the session intact — check with 'auth' afterwards rather than believing the navigation.

traps: A signed-OUT question page is full of a[href^="/profile/"] links — every answer author has one. An unscoped profile-link selector therefore reports every logged-out question page as signed in. The probe only accepts such a link inside the header/nav shell, and this is the single easiest way to get this file wrong.
Quora shows a partial answer and a 'continue reading' gate to signed-out visitors. Content coming back is not evidence of a session; truncated content is evidence of the opposite.
The session cookies are HttpOnly; the readable ones are set for anonymous visitors too, so no cookie here separates the two states.
notes: PROBE STRATEGY, in falling order of trust: (a) 'window.ansFrontendGlobals' — Quora's own front-end state object; if it names a viewer, that is the site's verdict, not ours. (b) an inline-script scan for the bootstrap's own logged-in boolean, because Quora ships a large JSON payload inline and a false there is as informative as a true. (c) a DOM check, LAST and scoped to the shell, for the reason in traps[0]. No cookie is read at any layer. Everything here is documentation-and-structure reasoning, not a live run: the exact key path under ansFrontendGlobals is the weakest link and is why status is 'unverified'. A READ RECIPE should target Quora's GraphQL-ish POST endpoint (/graphql/gql_para_POST) that the page itself calls with its own formkey/CSRF header, fetching a question's answers as JSON; DOM scraping fights the 'continue reading' gate and the virtualised answer list. WRITE is empty: answering and commenting are exactly the actions that get an account flagged as automated, and no reviewed write path exists here.
probe_checked: 2026-09-14: Go client `auth` ran live against the owner profile and returned a clean signed_out verdict (bootstrap logged-in flag false). Signed-OUT path proven again; signed-IN path still a hypothesis (profile is not signed in here).
